body:
There are 2 issues with your `starship.toml`

1. Everything is indented by 1 space character, particularly your `format` section. This is causing the `directory` portion of the prompt to be indented by 1 space.
2. The `format` of your `python` module has a trailing space. You probably have a `.py` file in `~`, triggering the python module, so it is inserting a space there before the `>` character.  The `~/code/repos/` directory likely does not have any `.py` files, so the space does not get inserted there.

Fix those two issues, and the problem should be resolved.

```toml
add_newline = false

format = """
$username\
$hostname\
$directory\
$git_branch\
$git_state\
$git_status\
$line_break\
$python\
$character"""

[directory]
style = "#88c0d0" # Lime

[character]
success_symbol = "[❯](#b48ead)" # Purple
error_symbol = "[❯](#bf616a)" # Red
vicmd_symbol = "[❮](#a3be8c)" # Green

[git_branch]
format = "[$branch]($style)"
style = "#d08770" # Orange

[git_status]
format = "[[(*$conflicted$untracked$modified$staged$renamed$deleted)](218) ($ahead_behind$stashed)]($style)"
style = "#5e81ac" # Cyan
conflicted = "​"
untracked = "​"
modified = "​"
staged = "​"
renamed = "​"
deleted = "​"
stashed = "≡"

[git_state]
format = "[[(*$conflicted$untracked$modified$staged$renamed$deleted)](218) ($ahead_behind$stashed)]($style)"
style = "#ebcb8b" # Yellow

[python]
format = "[$virtualenv]($style)"
style = "#ebcb8b" # Yellow
```

Thanks!
That was indeed the problem. I still wanted to have a white space after the python environment name only when an environment is active, but as you said the python module was triggering every time there was a `.py` file in the directory.

In case someone else has the same issue, I fixed it using a conditional format string:
```
[python]
format = "[($virtualenv )]($style)"
style = "#ebcb8b" # Yellow
```
